description: What the entity is chemically or biologically. Derived from source chemistry, not from role.

biological_types.definition: A non-polymer organic compound that is not primarily a lipid, ion, nucleotide or chromophore.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Non-polymer with heavy-atom count above the ion threshold and a CCD type of NON-POLYMER or similar.
biological_types.exclusion_rule: Excluded when the component is on the curated lipid, detergent, buffer or cryoprotectant list.
biological_types.decision_logic: Chemical class from the PDB Chemical Component Dictionary; never inferred from how often the component appears.

biological_types.definition: A short polymer of amino acids, whether modelled as its own chain or as a non-polymer.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Polymer entity of protein type below the peptide length threshold, or a source annotation of type 'peptide'.
biological_types.exclusion_rule: Not applied to a receptor chain or to a folded protein partner.
biological_types.decision_logic: Length is used only to separate peptide from protein, never to decide whether the chain is a ligand.

biological_types.inclusion_rule: Polymer entity of protein type at or above the peptide length threshold.
biological_types.exclusion_rule: Not applied to short peptide ligands.

biological_types.definition: A membrane lipid, sterol or lipidic mesophase component.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Component present on the curated lipid/sterol list, sourced from the CCD.
biological_types.exclusion_rule: A lipid that a source explicitly annotates as the structure's pharmacological ligand keeps this biological type but takes a pharmacological ligand_role.
biological_types.decision_logic: Biological type and role are independent axes: cholesterol is a lipid whether or not it is the ligand.

biological_types.definition: A nucleotide, nucleoside or close analogue.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: CCD parent or curated list membership.
biological_types.exclusion_rule: Not applied to nucleic-acid polymers, which are polymer chains.
biological_types.decision_logic: Relevant because in the Nucleotide family these are genuine ligands and in G-protein complexes (GDP, GTP analogues) they are cofactors of the transducer.

biological_types.definition: Retinal or another covalently attached chromophore.
biological_types.decision_logic: Separated from small_molecule because opsin chromophores are covalent and their pharmacology is a distinct question.

biological_types.definition: A monatomic or simple inorganic ion.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Curated ion list membership, or a CCD formula of a single element with a formal charge.
biological_types.decision_logic: Per OD-08 an ion is environment by default, including sodium in the 2x50 pocket.

biological_types.definition: A sugar or oligosaccharide, typically a glycan.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Branched entity, or curated saccharide list membership.
biological_types.decision_logic: Branched entities are carbohydrate by construction in this dataset.

biological_types.definition: A free amino acid or a fragment of two or three residues modelled as a non-polymer.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: CCD parent is a standard amino acid, or curated list membership.
biological_types.decision_logic: Kept distinct because a free amino acid can be a genuine ligand (e.g. at some sensory receptors) or a crystallisation additive.

biological_types.definition: A chemically identified entity that fits none of the above.
biological_types.inclusion_rule: Chemistry is known but outside the listed classes.

biological_types.definition: Chemistry could not be determined from available sources.

vocabulary_status.policy: A value outside this file may not appear in any Phase 2 artefact. The test suite fails on an unknown value rather than accepting it. Adding a value requires an entry in governance/DECISION_LOG.md.
